verdict.rationale: Requesty issues its own gateway API keys and service-account keys for non-human entities, each with its own monthly spend cap. Upstream provider keys can be held by Requesty via BYOK, so apps authenticate with a Requesty token rather than a raw provider key. Team-scoped key minting is not documented, and the claim that provider keys are never exposed is only implied by the gateway design. missing for 10: explicit team-level key issuance, documentation that provider keys are hidden from key holders, key lifecycle details (rotation/revocation), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can mint gateway-managed keys for teams and apps without exposing raw provider keys

citations.quote: Each API key or service account can have its own monthly spend cap.
Service accounts allow you create non-human entities... spend from those keys will not be tied to any user.
Bring Your Own Keys (BYOK) allows you to use your personal API keys from various providers with Requesty.
